payload.name: Preserve-Explicit-Subjective-Evaluations
payload.description: When a message states an event plus an explicit subjective evaluation or feeling about it (e.g., 'it was a huge success', 'I was relieved'), apply during extraction and memory updates to keep the evaluation in memory, not only the concrete event.
content: When a message contains both an event and an explicit subjective evaluation, feeling, or judgment about that event (e.g., 'jogging without pain was a huge success', 'I was thrilled'), extract and store the evaluation as well as the event itself; do not drop it because it is not a concrete action.
Represent the evaluation as its own memory candidate (e.g., an event or state about the speaker's assessment) or fold it into the event memory so the speaker's expressed feeling remains retrievable.
During CRUD, when evaluating extraction candidates or existing memories, do not merge away an explicit evaluation solely because the event it refers to is already recorded.

solves: Extraction captured only the concrete celebration event and dropped the speaker's explicit evaluation ('a huge success'), leaving later feeling questions unanswerable. The mechanism is omitting subjective evaluations when an event is present. Apply to any message pairing an event with an explicit feeling or judgment (relief, pride, disappointment) so feeling-related questions remain answerable.
